Fei Review

Pros

  • High draw efficiency and consistency.

  • Strong early turn burst with Signature Card and Ego Skill.

  • Lots of built-in synergy and flow within her own kit.

Cons

  • Requires specific teams and playstyles to play around Fei’s X-cost cards, if using them.

  • Fei’s high action count and hit count is punished by several different enemies.

  • No self-buffing capabilities, reliant on allies to deal optimal damage.

  • Can sometimes use or need a large amount of hand space because of creation, draw, and move effects.

Review

Introduction

Fei is a 5-Star Void Ranger combatant who lights the battlefield ablaze with her Inferno Rhapsody, extinguishing enemies and calling the heavens down upon them.

Fei's game plan revolves around her "Inferno Rhapsody" cards, which are created from "Exorcism Formation". Fei uses "Inferno Rhapsody" as a low-cost way to stack up her "Flame Arts" buff and draw cards while dishing out some moderate damage. When doing so, Fei will be firing off extra-attacks at enemies and generating stacks of "Descent" each time a card is drawn. Upon reaching 8 stacks of "Descent", - Fei will create a copy of "Heavensfall" in her hand to dish out even more damage.

As Fei wants to be drawing cards to generate her “Descent” stacks, you’ll want to be pairing her with combatants who can offer consistent deck cycling, as consistent cycling then turns into consistent damage. When drawing multiple cards via a single card, it will grant a stack of “Descent” for each card drawn. Pairing Fei with other combatants who can draw multiple cards at a time will push Fei’s potential damage output, think units such as Veronica or Beryl. As Fei does bring some solid card draw of her own via her “Soliloquy” and “Soulfire Dance” cards, she is able to fulfill her “Descent” buff quite self-sufficiently. 

The majority of Fei’s damage comes from her Attack-Cards “Inferno Rhapsody” and “Heavensfall” - with some extra damage coming from an Extra Attack when Fei reaches 3 stacks of “Flame Arts”. As all of Fei’s attacks have relatively low base damage values and multiple of Fei’s Attack-cards are also multi-hitters. As Fei offers few forms of self-buffing from her cards themselves, pairing Fei with supporting combatants who can offer additive damage buffs, such as Morale, will help elevate her damage to the next level, think of units like Rei.

Fei can be built to be played as a sub-DPS with some of the epiphanies offered in her kit due to her low-cost cards and in-built card draw, but as Fei creates multiple pseudo-bricks in the draw pile, it can somewhat reduce her effectiveness in that role, better positioning her to be your primary carry. Fei also utilizes cards that have an “X” cost, as these cards consume all AP. It’s important to have forethought to ensure you’re planning your turn accordingly to maximize their output and avoid awkward situations where you don’t want to use all of your remaining AP for the turn.

Fei's main weaknesses are her low damage values and high action count due to the nature of her card spam. Buffs on enemies such as Fortitude will significantly hinder her damage unless paired with other combatants who can offer substantial damage buffs. On top of this, due to the amount of card draw and card creation, hand size can become a factor you’ll need to play around with as well. 

When coming into Chaos or Sortie, Fei brings enough utility of her own to function well enough without being too reliant on other combatants. However, Fei doesn’t absolutely steamroll through this content due to her lower base values, but still dishes out plenty of damage on her own. You’ll still be wanting to look for and pair her with combatants who help with her lower base values. 

Review

Key Mechanics

Fei’s playstyle is all about using her “Inferno Rhapsody” Attack-Cards to build up stacks of her “Flame Arts” buff. Once Fei reaches 3 stacks of “Flame Arts”, she will deal a random extra-attack to an enemy and then will lose all stacks of “Flame Arts”. On top of this, Fei wants to draw cards each turn to stack her “Descent” buff to 8. Upon reaching 8 stacks of “Descent”, Fei creates a “Heavensfall” in her hand and removes 8 stacks of “Descent”. 

  • Inferno Rhapsody - Inferno Rhapsody is a 0-Cost Attack Card that deals 70% damage to a single enemy and grants a singular stack of the buff “Flame Arts”. If this card grants the 3rd stack of “Flame Arts”, while also drawing you a card. Fei’s standard way to generate stacks of her “Flame Arts” buff, providing solid damage and the ability to fuel Descent stacks.

  • Flame Arts - The “Flame Arts” effect that is granted via Fei’s cards doesn’t provide any inherent effect; instead, when it reaches 3 stacks, Fei will fire off an Extra Attack at a random enemy, dealing 120% damage and removing 3 stacks. 

  • Descent - Descent is a buff that Fei can obtain through her “Exorcism Formation” card and by her “Inferno Rhapsody: Heaven” cards, stacking up to 8 times. When Fei reaches 8 stacks of “Descent”, she will remove all stacks and create a copy of “Heavensfall” in her hand. Extremely important to try and stack up as much as possible, as a large portion of Fei’s damage comes from her “Heavensfall” card. 

  • Heavensfall - A 0-Cost Attack card that has the [Ephemeral] and [Exhaust] tags, deals 100% damage to a single enemy 3 times. This is where a large amount of Fei’s damage comes from. This card can only be created up to a maximum of 10 times per turn, however.

  • Inferno Rhapsody: Heaven - An alternative variant of Fei’s standard “Inferno Rhapsody” card that can be obtained via the 5th Epiphany on “Exorcism Formation”. This variant deals slightly more base damage, still costing 0-AP to cast and grants 1 stack of “Flame Arts”, but dealing 110% Damage instead. When “Inferno Rhapsody: Heaven” grants the 3rd stack of “Flame Arts”, instead of drawing a card, it will instead grant 3 stacks of “Descent”. This variant lowers Feis potential draw output but significantly increases Fei's potential “Heavensfall” generation.

Utilizing Exorcism Formation IV, Fei now does twice the Extra Attacks for every [Flame Art] activation, which can be broken down as now doing 2 Extra Attacks for every 3 Inferno Rhapsody. With Soulfire Dance V also in deck, this means that Fei does 3 Extra Attacks for every 3 Inferno Rhapsody, or 50% of her hits. This is important as Extra Attacks scale better than normal hits, which gives half of her damage an extra edge. Night Rain IV is crucial for off-setting potential bad draw from excessive Inferno Rhapsody since it’s guaranteed at the start of turn but it requires you to use 'Common Draw' effects--the divines can be replaced with AP Divines if your team needs that more heavily. It's recommended to use Fei alongside Nia with Forbidden: Hunger (alongside a buffer) with this deck (or another form of high AP like Tiphera) since the X-cost can be quite expensive without it. One Night Rain IV can be dropped to gain Neutral cards as well.

Because Night Rain IV moves to hand at start of turn, it doesn’t have to be manually drawn and therefore draw divines on it become ‘pure’ draw that are much more efficient than alternatives. In any team that doesn’t have excessive [Retain] or Start of Turn Create/[Move] effects, Fei can be an extremely competitive and consistent Draw Unit especially with units like Tenebria who often have the highest likelihood of a bad draw early in the turn, rather than later, since Fei’s Start of Turn [Move] circumvents these issues. The major drawback is the need to have a lot of Common Draw Divines or Common Cards on allies or Fei won't have draw targets.
Synergies

Fei Synergies

Hugo
  • Fei plays a decent number of attacks and also a decent number of skills, making Fei a competitive Hugo driver.
  • While Fei can drive Hugo relatively well, the team can be lacking in buffs, and she will also struggle to activate the Extra Attack engrave of S3 consistently (make 5 cards a turn). It often will be recommended to use cards like Negotiation when playing them together which can have big drawbacks to consider.
Nia
  • Nia with Forbidden: Hunger can make the highest amount of draw and AP in the game, all from one unit. When playing a unit who might use X-cost cards, as Fei incentivizes, Nia is an extremely efficient ally.
  • Nia can also be used to manipulate what cards certain effects from Fei draw. For example, some effects on Fei require next draw to be 0-cost or Inferno Rhapsody, Nia’s Adagio can manipulate Fei cards to top-of-draw in order to get the most out of these interactions.
Cassius
  • Cassius is a generically strong buffer and high recommendation for most multi-hit units like Fei.
  • Cassius’ Empowered Quest Upgrade activates at start-of-turn, which gives a 75% chance of drawing 1. This additional draw can lessen the odds of bad Inferno Rhapsody rng almost completely in many Fei builds and vastly increase her consistency.
Rei
  • Rei, while behind Cassius in top-level buff strength, has exclusive buffs to Void units and 0 to 1-cost cards that Fei can make great use of.
  • Rei also has the benefit of very strong T1’s, which will make her preferred in a lot of content over Cassius, despite her lower top-end strength for a lot of players.

Fei Seasonal Powers

Introduces Desire Cards. Desire Cards are cards that primarily exist to give a strong passive buff from meeting certain Desire Thresholds (3/5/7) which can only be done by having multiple ally decks also made in Season-4. 

  • For Desire Threshold, it’s common to run 1 Claim / 1 Survival / 1 Inquiry for use in a variety of builds; however, it's also common to just do 3 ‘X’ to meet effect easier or do 2 'X' / 1 Inquiry (to keep Sample Collection as Card Effect). This is extremely dependent on ally desire cards and individual team building goal.

’X’ refers to a ‘Placeholder for Specific Desire Threshold Goal’, i.e. if you are building your team for 7 Claim then you might do 2 Claim / 1 Inquiry.

Introduces Persona Cards and Engravings. Persona Cards are powerful cards that introduce new playstyles or ways of buffing/debuffing. Engravings are effects that can be applied to both the Persona Cards and Equipment, functioning near identically to Refinements of Season-2 but with new effects.

  • The most common Card Engraving to take for Attack Persona Cards is [For each Lux Engraving, 1 Mark to random enemies ] or [Attunement: Decrease Cost by 1 until used].

    • For Skill Persona Cards [When this card is Discarded, activate this card] is the recommended choice, provided you are playing this unit with a way to facilitate its discard. 

  • The most common Equipment Engraving to optimize for is [When 5 or more cards have been created through abilities by allies, +30% Damage Amount to Extra Attacks of this unit (1 time per turn)]. This effect stacks. But, other damage increase effects are viable just significantly worse for Extra Attack units than the dedicated Engraving.

Introduces Refinements, effects on Equipment that allow one to get additional Equipment effects for no Faint-Cost (post-S2), and God’s Hammer, a powerful effect that gives a random copy of any other Equipment effect on-top of current Equipment but costs 10 Faint Memory and is only gained from the Boss.

  • Increase Damage Amount of Attack Cards by 20%.

  • +30% Damage Amount of 1-cost or lower Attack Cards.

  • Increase Damage Amount of Extra Attacks by 25%.

Because God’s Hammer is completely RNG at the end of the run, we do not have a specific recommendation since the player has very little control over the decision but for ATK-based Attackers usually ATK% gear is considered best and DEF-based Attackers DEF% gear is considered best.

Introduces Forbidden Cards, powerful cards that create new synergies and can only be acquired once per run (can be duped at one event or via save data editing). 

  • Forbidden: Gesture of Freedom. Permanent Cost-Reduction to  one card, can be manipulated.

  • Forbidden: Portrait of Fury. ++Draw, +Damage

  • Forbidden: Ecstasy of Violence. +Damage

  • Forbidden: Eternal Hunger. +Draw, ++AP (Ally Reliant)
